## Key terms

{{< glossary hallucination knowledge-cutoff ai-claim fact-checking reliable-source lateral-reading citation made-up-source ai-bias stereotype >}}

## 21.1 Why an AI answer can be wrong

- It **predicts likely words**, it does not look every fact up.
- It has a **knowledge cutoff** and does not know your local facts.
- It **sounds sure**, even when it invents (**hallucination**).

![Why an AI answer can be wrong.](images/why-wrong.png){width=100%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
A source in the answer does not prove anything: it may be invented.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Lab task · Ask and doubt"}
Ask an AI for "five facts about sleep and memory, with sources". Highlight
every number, name, date and source.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Reasons"}
Choose the reason for the mistake.

::: {.match extra="a slow Internet|a small screen"}
“Our college library opens at 7:00.”
:   it cannot know local facts

“The newest laptop is …” (from two years ago)
:   the knowledge cutoff

a study that does not exist
:   a hallucination

a wrong number in a sure voice
:   it predicts likely words
:::
:::

## 21.2 Find the claims and check them

- **Find** claims: numbers, dates, names, quotes, "studies show".
- **Check** each in **two reliable sources** (**lateral reading**).
- **Decide:** true → keep; wrong → correct; cannot check → remove.

![Find the claims, then check each one.](images/check-claims.png){width=100%}

{{< sim file="sims/fact-check-lab.html" poster="sims/fact-check-lab.png" title="Fact-Check Lab: Sami's AI draft" height="620" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Do not check the AI with the same AI.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Lab task · Check three claims"}
Decide about all six claims in **Fact-Check Lab**. Then check three claims of
your own document with two sources each.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Decisions"}
Use Fact-Check Lab. Choose the decision.

::: {.match extra="ask the AI again|keep it"}
“The brain uses 50 % of the body's energy.”
:   correct it to about 20 %

“Adults need at least 7 hours of sleep.”
:   true: keep it

“Einstein said: Sleep is the best study.”
:   cannot check: remove it

“The library opens at 7:00.”
:   correct it to 8:00
:::
:::

## 21.3 Made-up sources and quotes

- A **citation**: author, title, year, where to find it.
- Three checks: **search the title**, **search the authors and the
  journal**, **open the link or DOI**.
- All fail → a **made-up source**: delete it or find a real one.

![Three quick checks of a source.](images/fake-source.png){width=100%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Quote websites often copy each other: find the original.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Lab task · Test two sources"}
Ask an AI for three studies about sleep and exams. Check two with the three
checks: real or made up?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Sources"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="the font of the title|the colour of the link"}
the first check of a source
:   search the title

no such journal exists
:   a made-up source

what to do with a made-up source
:   delete it or find a real one

the parts of a citation
:   author, title, year, where
:::
:::

## 21.4 Bias in AI texts and pictures

- **AI bias:** unfair ideas about groups, **stereotypes**, or one side only.
- Ask for **neutral language**, **different people**, **both sides**.
- Read again: who is shown, who is missing?

![Bias.](images/bias.png){width=100%}

{{< sim file="sims/bias-lab.html" poster="sims/bias-lab.png" title="Bias Lab: who does the AI show, and how?" height="560" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
An AI learned from people's texts: it is not automatically neutral.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Lab task · A fair text"}
Fix the three requests in **Bias Lab**. Then rewrite an AI job ad for a
warehouse worker so that it describes the job, not the person.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Bias"}
Use Bias Lab. Choose the instruction that helps.

::: {.match extra="write longer|use more emojis"}
“the doctor, a confident man; the nurse, a kind young woman”
:   use neutral language

“the IT trainee is a young man who loves games”
:   show different people

“remote work is always better”
:   give both sides with reasons

“a strong young man for the warehouse”
:   describe the job, not the person
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Claim Court {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

Six AI answers: a **wrong number**, a **made-up study**, an **outdated**
laptop, a **biased** job ad, a **one-sided** opinion, and a **wrong sum**.

{{< sim file="sims/claim-court.html" poster="sims/claim-court.png" title="Claim Court: judge the AI answers" kind="game" height="520" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · The verdicts"}
Choose the verdict.

::: {.match extra="true: keep it|ask the AI again"}
the brain uses 50 %
:   wrong: correct it

Miller & Hart (2019)
:   made up: delete it

the newest laptop, from an old AI
:   maybe outdated: check a current source

75 + 50 + 60 = 195
:   wrong sum: compute it yourself
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 6 · Good habits (harder)"}
Choose the habit.

::: {.match extra="trust the sure voice|use one blog"}
before you use an AI number
:   check two reliable sources

before you use an AI source
:   search it and open it

before you use an AI text about people
:   check for stereotypes

before you use an AI table
:   recompute the sums
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- AI predicts likely words, has a cutoff and sounds sure.
- Find the claims; check each in two reliable sources; keep, correct or
  remove.
- Check every source: title, authors and journal, link.
- Ask for neutral language and both sides; read again for bias.
